summary: Antigua and Barbuda waives visas for more than 100 nationalities, including the US, Canada, the UK, the EU and most Commonwealth countries, normally for stays of up to six months — while CARICOM nationals move freely and everyone else applies for an eVisa online (or at a mission) before traveling, unless they hold a US, Canadian, UK or Schengen visa, which qualifies them for a USD 100 visa on arrival.

AF.notes: Apply for a visitor visa in advance, online through the Immigration Department’s eVisa system (decision within seven working days) or at an Antigua and Barbuda mission; arriving without one can mean a fine or refused entry. Holders of a valid US, Canadian, UK or Schengen visa or residence card can instead get a 30-day Tourist Visa-on-Arrival for USD 100.

conditionalWaivers.text: Travellers who need a visa but hold a valid US, Canadian, UK or Schengen visa or residence card can get a single-entry Tourist Visa-on-Arrival for up to 30 days, for USD 100 per passenger (children included). It is for tourism or visiting friends and relatives only, cannot be extended or converted except on medical grounds, and requires a passport valid for six months, a return ticket and enough money for the stay.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required from travelers aged one year and over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, including after more than 12 hours' transit through an airport in one. WHO's risk list includes Trinidad and Tobago, so a Caribbean origin does not by itself exempt you.

travelInsurance.text: No official source makes insurance a condition of entry for ordinary visits. The UK government advises adequate travel health insurance: treatment can be expensive and serious cases may need an emergency evacuation.

onwardTicket.text: Visitors must hold a return or onward ticket; immigration officers also ask for the address where you are staying and set the length of stay accordingly.

proofOfFunds.text: Visitors must be able to show evidence that they can maintain themselves during their stay, alongside an onward or return ticket and confirmed accommodation. No fixed amount is published.

declarations.name: ArriveAntigua online arrival form
declarations.text: The authorities advise travelers to complete the ArriveAntigua form online to speed up entry. It is not mandatory, and it can only be filled in on a phone or tablet within 72 hours of travel.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Antigua and Barbuda travel advice (entry requirements)

currencyLimits.text: On arrival you must declare cash, cheques or money orders worth more than USD 10,000 or the equivalent in other currencies, according to Canada's travel advice. No Antiguan government page we could read states the threshold.

notes: The UK Foreign Office says there are strict rules on goods you can take into or out of Antigua and Barbuda, and you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.
Canada's travel advice says it is an offence to wear camouflage clothing or to carry or import items made from camouflage material; items are confiscated and offenders can be fined or jailed.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says the currency is the East Caribbean dollar (XCD) and that US dollars are widely accepted. No official source we could read describes card acceptance.

safety.text: Antigua and Barbuda is a calm destination for visitors; the usual issues are opportunistic theft from beaches and rental cars, and strong currents on the Atlantic coast. Hurricane season runs from June to November.

tips.text: Canada's travel advice says an International Driving Permit is not recognized; you need a temporary local driver's licence, bought on presentation of your home licence. The UK Foreign Office says car hire companies usually help, or you can get one from the Transport Board or a police station. Traffic drives on the left.

Canada's travel advice says the hurricane season runs from early June to the end of November, and that even small tropical storms can quickly become major hurricanes. Take travel insurance that covers weather disruption if you travel then.
Canada's travel advice says US dollars are widely accepted. The UK Foreign Office says taxis are not metered and fares are set by zone: agree the fare in local currency before you set off.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Antigua and Barbuda?
faq.answer: Probably not. Antigua and Barbuda waives visas for more than 100 nationalities, including the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, the EU and most Commonwealth countries — visitors are normally admitted for up to six months. CARICOM nationals move freely. Everyone else needs a visitor visa before traveling, applied for online through the Immigration Department’s eVisa system or at an Antigua and Barbuda mission. Travellers who hold a valid US, Canadian, UK or Schengen visa or residence card can instead buy a 30-day Tourist Visa-on-Arrival for USD 100.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Antigua and Barbuda without a visa?
faq.answer: Immigration officers grant the length of stay they think your trip needs, up to six months for most visa-free visitors. Ask for what you actually need at the desk — extending later means a trip to the Immigration Department in St John's and a fee.

faq.question: How much passport validity do I need?
faq.answer: Officially your passport must be valid for the duration of your stay. Airlines frequently apply their own six-month rule, so renew if you have less than six months left.

faq.question: Do I need a return ticket?
faq.answer: Yes. Visitors are expected to hold a confirmed onward or return ticket and to give an address in Antigua or Barbuda. Both are commonly checked at the immigration desk.

faq.question: Can I work remotely from Antigua and Barbuda?
faq.answer: Yes — the Nomad Digital Residence lets remote workers and their families live in Antigua and Barbuda for up to two years. It costs USD 1,500 for a single applicant, USD 2,000 for a couple and USD 3,000 for a family of up to four (USD 650 for each additional person), and requires proof of remote income plus medical and travel insurance for the full two years. Short visa-free visits do not permit local employment.
